description.narrative: (Cambodia): The Inclusive Primary Education (IPEA) activity supports the national scale-up of the early grade learning program, which leverages investments of other USG resources (non-bilateral) through coordination with the Global Partnership for Education, the Ministry of Education, Youth, and Sports, international and local non-government organizations, the private sector, and development partners. This activity will improve the early grade reading skills of children with and without disabilities in primary schools in Cambodia by implementing a national roll-out of the Inclusive Early Grade Learning program, and strengthen school governance, transparency, and accountability. It will also invest heavily in strengthening school governance, transparency and accountability by engaging and empowering parents, school communities and local leaders...USAID awarded this activity to Research Triangle Institute (RTI International) through a competitive process, in accordance with federal procurement regulations...By providing early grade learning programs to all students throughout Cambodia and ensuring no child is left behind, IPEA contributes to USAID/Cambodia's CDCS 2020-2025 Development Objective 2 "Health, education, and welfare of Cambodians improved through enhanced services,'' the USG Education Strategy's Objective 1, "Improve learning outcomes'' and Objective 2 "Expand access to quality basic education for all, Particularly Marginalized and Vulnerable Populations," as well as to USAID's Education Policy "Children and youth gain literacy, numeracy, and social-emotional skills that are foundational to future learning and success." In addition, this activity supports the ICS Mission Objective 2.3, Sub-objective 2.3.3, "By the end of 2023, national partners increase resilience of education systems and child protection services, reducing inequities in learning and access.".. ...
